reason: BDB cites an Arabic cognate for the root of אֱנוֹשׁ ('be inclined, friendly, social'; Nöldeke: denominative), which meets ¶24's sense of intimacy against wildness, while Hebrew usage of enosh stresses mortality (Ps 103:15, Ps 90:3) and a homonymous אָנַשׁ means 'be incurable' (Jer 17:9, Jer 15:18): used at ¶24. The pupil אִישׁוֹן ('little man of the eye' in Strong; BDB derives אִישׁ uncertainly, possibly from אנשׁ) carries ¶23's insān al-ʿayn image: used at ¶23. Aramaic אֱנָשׁ (sound correspondence only) appears in Dan 7:13 but shares no scene (elenen at ¶20). אִשָּׁה, אֵשׁ and אִשֶּׁה, grouped under the root in the lexicon, are false friends for this page (the fire of Exod 3:2 is not linked to ānastu by root). Hebrew אנס 'compel' and Aramaic אנס 'oppress' (one occurrence each) add nothing.

Sound correspondence only (no BDB Arabic note). Hebrew חקק 'cut in, inscribe, decree'; חֹק/חֻקָּה 'statute, something prescribed, due portion' across 254 WLC occurrences, overwhelmingly legal 'statutes'. The sense 'fixed term or limit due to a person' (Job 14:5 ketiv חקו, qere חקיו; cf. Job 14:13) matches ¶12's last sentence on the day that brings each person to his term: used at ¶12. The page's other ḥaqq senses (truth, a strike that does not deviate, ¶18) have no Hebrew counterpart in this root.

Hebrew and Aramaic חסר by sound correspondence only (BDB gives no Arabic note). Range over 60 WLC occurrences: decrease (Gen 8:3,5 waters), lack/want/poverty (Prov 28:22, Deut 8:9), 'lacking sense' (Proverbs), deficiency that cannot be counted (Eccl 1:15); Aramaic חַסִּיר 'found lacking' on the scales (Dan 5:27). It shares the page's base sense of diminution (¶5) and the scale image (¶12) but lacks the Arabic senses of commercial loss of capital, straying and perishing; those appear in Syriac ḥsar/ḥusrānā only as reported by Corpus Coranicum. Used at ¶3 (Ps 8:6 'made him lack little'), ¶5, ¶7 (Prov 28:22), ¶12 (Dan 5:27), ¶25 (Eccl 4:8 'depriving myself'). Hebrew חשר (BDB's Arabic cognate there is 'collect', ḥ-š-r) is a false friend (2Sam 22:12 rejected).

Hebrew צבר means 'heap up' (grain Gen 41:35,49; silver Job 27:16; Ps 39:7 'he heaps up and knows not who gathers'); sound correspondence only, no lexicon note. Arabic ṣabr is patience/endurance. The heaping verses touch ¶9's hoarding, but through the sense 'heap', not through ṣabr; they were rejected as duplicates of Luke 12:16-21. No annotation rests on the root.

Hebrew עצר (63 occurrences) means restrain, retain, shut up (wombs Gen 20:18, heavens Deut 11:17, waters Job 12:15, a plague stayed Ps 106:30, detained 1Sam 21:8) and עֲצָרָה 'solemn assembly'; sound correspondence only. The senses the page draws from ʿaṣr (squeezing, long time and late day, refuge, lineage) are absent; 'withholding water' is even the reverse of squeezing it out. The three candidate verses were rejected.

Sound correspondence only. Hebrew עמל (76 occurrences) is wearisome toil, trouble, mischief (Job, Psalms), concentrated in Qohelet, where toil yields no surplus (Eccl 1:3, 2:11) and the lone toiler deprives himself (4:8); Ps 90:10 pairs it with emptiness. The Arabic ʿamal of 103:3 is 'deed', the very thing that escapes loss. Used to make the difference visible at ¶6 (karsi_anlati) and quoted at ¶9 (Ps 90:10).

The lexicon has no Hebrew or Aramaic root with corresponding consonants (cognates tool: none). The Hebrew Bible expresses enjoining by צוה (מִצְוָה, as in Avot 2:1), which is not a regular sound correspondent of w-ṣ-y (memory, unverified); no parallel is built on it for 103:2.
